title: Operator proofing and audit sampling proposal
summary: Draft proposal for a lightweight operator proofing standard and audit-sampling framework for customer-managed networking change approvals. Aims to balance evidence fidelity for audits with operational cost and customer privacy. Intended as an extension to approval-gate workflows in Private Deployments.
goals: Define a minimal, tamper-evident evidence bundle format operators must produce for VPC change approvals
Specify sampling and retention policy tiers to reduce storage costs while meeting common compliance needs
Provide API surface for customers and Redwood SREs to fetch, validate, and replay evidence bundles
Integrate optional cryptographic attestations for customer-managed components (signed by customer KMS/HSM)
Produce a rollout plan: canary with selective customers, instrumentation, and SLOs for approval latency impact
requirements: REQ-1: Every approval decision (allow/deny/escalate) must produce an immutable evidence bundle for the change request ID

REQ-2: Evidence bundle MUST include a timestamp, actor identity (Redwood operator ID + customer-provided actor if present), affected resources, delta (before/after), and routing context (region, tenant id)
REQ-3: Evidence bundle schema should be compact JSON-LD plaintext and accompanied by an optional compressed pcap or syslog excerpt for network changes
REQ-4: Evidence bundles must be content-addressed (SHA-256) and recorded in an append-only index with retention tags
REQ-5: Support three retention tiers: short (30d), standard (180d), extended (2y) configurable per-customer and per-change-class
REQ-6: Sampling policy configurable by customer: deterministic (every Nth), risk-driven (heatmap-based), and policy-driven (critical routes always captured)
REQ-7: Expose evidence retrieval APIs that accept request ID or time window; support signed URL export with RBAC checks
REQ-8: When customers opt-in, ingest customer-signed attestations (PKCS#7 or JWS) verifying the on-prem operator action; Redwood verifies signature using customer-provided public keys stored in KMS
REQ-9: Approvals service must annotate any approvals impacted by sampling (e.g., partial evidence) and show confidence score in the Console
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: End-to-end create -> approval -> evidence bundle stored and retrievable via API for a sample change in staging
AC-2: Evidence bundles are content-addressed and immutable; retrieval returns exact copy with matching hash
AC-3: Sampling policy can be updated via admin UI and takes effect within a defined deployment window (<= 5 minutes for policy sync)
AC-4: Console shows per-change evidence availability, retention tier, and confidence metadata
AC-5: Customer-provided signed attestations are successfully validated in 3 tested key formats
AC-6: Performance impact on approval latency must be < 150ms median for standard retention settings (measured in dedicated canary)
detailed-design-notes: High-level approach: produce an evidence bundle at the point of decision. Bundle is small by default (meta + succinct diff), with optional payload attachments stored in compressed blobs. Use content-addressed storage (CAS) for blobs; index entries point to hashes. Index is append-only and versioned. For customer-managed networking we allow a ‘customer-attestation’ field: a string containing a JWS or PKCS#7 signature produced by the customer on a canonical serialization of the diff + request-id. If present, Redwood verifies against public keys supplied during onboarding. Sampling: implement a sampling orchestrator as a policy engine that attaches sampling tags to change requests; this engine consults a risk-scoring function (traffic, route criticality, recent churn) and configured sampling rules. For low-risk changes we store only the summary; for high-risk changes we preserve full syslog/pcap snippets (heuristic cap at 5MB).
evidence-bundle-example:
{
  "request_id": "req_20250301_8af4",
  "timestamp": "2025-02-28T18:12:03Z",
  "actor": "op-pri-23",
  "customer_actor": "customer-admin:alice@acme.com",
  "change_summary": "Added route 10.4.0.0/16 -> peering-zyx",
  "delta": "before: route missing; after: route added",
  "attachments": ["sha256:abcd..."],
  "signature": "jws:eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIs...",
  "sampling_tier": "standard"
}
retention_and_cost_model: Propose default: standard (180d) for all customers, opt-down to short if cost governance requested, opt-up for enterprise legal holds. Rough cost estimate: storing compact bundles (avg 2 KB) x 100k changes/month ~ 200 MB/mo; full attachments at 3 MB avg for 5% of changes ~ 15 GB/mo. We will add an admin cost control page showing predicted monthly storage by tier and allow retention overrides per-tenant. Consider lifecycle policy to archive extended-tier bundles to cold storage (S3 Glacier) after 90 days to reduce hot costs.
privacy_and_data_classification: Evidence bundles may contain customer-sensitive identifiers and small snippets of logs. Default redaction: mask any IPv6/IPv4 addresses in attachments unless customer opts into full capture. Provide a data classification toggle at onboarding: PII-minimal vs PII-full-capture. All bundles encrypted at rest with per-tenant KMS keys. Access logged and auditable.
operational_workflow: 1) Operator initiates change request -> 2) Approval flow executes (auto/manual) -> 3) On decision, approval service constructs evidence bundle -> 4) Bundle pushed to CAS and index entry appended -> 5) If customer-attestation present, verify and record validation result -> 6) Metrics emitted to Console and tracing recorded. Rollback: provide playbook entry to follow if an evidence bundle fails verification (escalate, re-run, preserve old state).
monitoring_and_slos: Instrument these metrics: evidence_generation_time, evidence_upload_latency, evidence_validation_failures, sampling_rate_by_rule, retrieval_latency. SLO targets: evidence_generation_time P50 < 100ms, P95 < 400ms; retrieval P95 < 1s for bundles in hot storage. Alerting: >1% validation failures for 1h => page oncall.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal staging tests (2 weeks) with synthetic customers. Phase 1: opt-in canary with 5 pilot customers (network-focused accounts) — gather cost/latency telemetry (4 weeks). Phase 2: soft default for new customers (90 days). Phase 3: full default for all new deployments and migration window for existing customers (6 months) with retention upgrade discounts. Include Customer Success playbook and technical checklist for customers who want to enable customer-signed attestations.
risks_and_open_questions: RQ-1: Is JSON-LD sufficient for legal/audit teams in regulated industries or do we need a normalized binary binding?
RQ-2: Legal may demand longer retention for certain customers; what is the cost share model for >2y retention?
RQ-3: Customer KMS integration: supported key formats and rotation semantics need alignment with Security
RQ-4: Sampling correctness: how to prove absence (i.e., that a change was sampled-out) to auditors without leaking too much metadata?
RQ-5: Operational burden if customers widely opt into full pcap capture — how to throttle attachments per tenant?
